- **self**: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials (16/5)

## Structure and components

- [statement] The EJS ACT-PD consortium describes a multi-arm, multi-stage (MAMS) platform trial design that will start with one placebo and three treatment arms, each with 400 participants, with a primary endpoint at 3 years powered to detect a 30% reduction in rate of progression of MDS-UPDRS Part I and II summed scores, with ineffective arms closed. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-22) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13616524/ · keywords: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials

## How it works

- [statement] Ahlskog and Uitti argue that interpretation of the ADAGIO rasagiline delayed-start trials is problematic because of divergent results with the 2 symptomatically beneficial doses and variability in UPDRS scores with active rasagiline that was twice the magnitude of the major finding. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2865777/ · keywords: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Recent reviews state that no disease-modifying therapy for Parkinson's disease has been established: one says there are currently no disease-modifying therapies (DMTs), and a trial-pipeline analysis says there are still no treatments to modify the course of the disease. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-17) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-026-01483-9 · keywords: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13442941/
- [statement] A ClinicalTrials.gov-based analysis of Parkinson's disease drug trials registered between 2015–2024 reports 444 trials, of which 42% were in Phase 1, 46% in Phase 2 and 12% in Phase 3, with 63% evaluating symptomatic therapies and 37% testing disease-modifying therapies. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-26) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13442941/ · keywords: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
- [statement] Mari and Mestre describe a “valley of death” in Parkinson's disease modification populated by failures such as the various NET-PD trials, the ADAGIO trial, the more recent α-Synuclein immunotherapy trials and the Ven-glustat trial. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8920063/ · keywords: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
- [statement] Isradipine evidence is split: the STEADY-PD III report concluded that isradipine did not slow clinical progression, while a re-analysis of STEADY-PD II data reports significantly smaller total and part 3 UPDRS scores with 10 mg/day ER isradipine than placebo at trial end, with post hoc adjustment for symptomatic therapy diminishing the statistical significance. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7465126/ · keywords: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8922308/
- [statement] In FAIRPARK-II (NCT02655315), a phase 2 trial in participants with newly diagnosed Parkinson's disease who had never received levodopa, the authors report that the mean MDS-UPDRS total score worsened by 15.6 points with deferiprone and 6.3 points with placebo (difference, 9.3 points; 95% confidence interval, 6.3 to 12.2; P<0.001) at 36 weeks, and the trial team's statement likewise reports greater deterioration with deferiprone than with placebo. (high confidence) — https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2209254 · keywords: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials · also: https://cureparkinsons.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/FAIRPARK-II-Statement-from-the-clinical-trial-team.pdf
- [statement] The FAIRPARK-II trial team's statement says that 4 other independent deferiprone trials involving about 240 people with Parkinson's disease, in which all participants were already receiving dopamine replacement drugs, observed no worsening of symptoms, and that this difference is probably where the explanation for the conflicting results lies. (low confidence) — https://cureparkinsons.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/FAIRPARK-II-Statement-from-the-clinical-trial-team.pdf · keywords: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
- [statement] Reviewers report that disease-modification trials in neurodegenerative disorders have struggled to separate symptomatic effects of putative agents from disease modification, and that documenting a disease-modifying effect is difficult for a Parkinson's disease drug with symptomatic benefit. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4910262/ · keywords: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2865777/
- [statement] A systematic review that searched 1980–2015 included 128 RCTs (84 in AD, 44 in PD) and concluded that none of the included studies convincingly demonstrated disease-modification. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4910262/ · keywords: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
- [statement] A PRISMA-compliant review of phase II and III disease-modifying trials (2020-2025) with at least one target-engagement biomarker included 26 trials (PD=19, MSA=4, DLB=3); the authors report that only 8/26 studies demonstrated both target engagement and statistically significant clinical benefit and that nine trials showed target engagement without clinical benefit. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42861702/ · keywords: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials
- [statement] Authors of two reviews attribute the lack of success of disease-modification trials to factors including the complexity of Parkinson's disease, variability between patients and biomarkers for stratification, advanced pathology at diagnosis, insensitive clinical endpoints and scales, and intervention timing in advanced stages of neurodegeneration. (medium confidence) — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-026-01483-9 · keywords: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13435201/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] SURE-PD3 (NCT02642393), a phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of inosine in early Parkinson's disease, randomized 298 participants and closed early after a prespecified interim futility analysis; the authors report MDS-UPDRS progression of 11.1 points per year with inosine versus 9.9 with placebo (P = .18). (high confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34519802/ · keywords: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials · also: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT02642393
- [statement] STEADY-PD III (NCT02168842), a phase 3 trial that randomized 336 patients with early Parkinson's disease to isradipine 5 mg twice daily or placebo for 36 months, reported adjusted least-squares mean changes in total UPDRS of 2.99 versus 3.26 points (treatment effect —0.27; P = 0.85), and its authors conclude that isradipine did not slow clinical progression. (high confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7465126/ · keywords: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials · also: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT02168842
- [statement] In the SPARK phase 2 trial (NCT03318523) of cinpanemab in early Parkinson's disease, the authors report the trial was stopped after the week 72 interim analysis owing to lack of efficacy, with a week 52 change in MDS-UPDRS of 10.8 points in the control group versus 10.5, 11.3 and 10.9 points in the 250-mg, 1250-mg and 3500-mg groups. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35921450/ · keywords: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials · also: https://www.michaeljfox.org/news/news-context-two-study-outcomes-disappoint-parkinsons-pipeline-remains-strong

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The STEADY-PD III authors state that the isradipine dose may have been insufficient to engage the target calcium channels associated with neuroprotective effects. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7465126/ · keywords: Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials

## Research summary — Disease-modification trial landscape and lessons from failed trials

Recent reviews state that no disease-modifying therapy for Parkinson's disease has been established. This concept collects registry and journal results from trials that did not show disease modification (SURE-PD3 inosine, STEADY-PD III isradipine, FAIRPARK-II deferiprone, SPARK cinpanemab) and, separately, the reasons reviewers give for such failures: symptomatic effects confound disease-modification readouts, delayed-start interpretation is contested, target engagement rarely coincided with clinical benefit in one review, and authors cite patient variability, late-stage pathology and insensitive endpoints. It also notes a post hoc re-analysis that disputes a clean negative reading of isradipine and a proposed multi-arm, multi-stage platform trial.
